question: In 1662, who described the equation P1V1 = P2V2, where P1 and V1 are the initial pressure and volume values, and P2 and V2 are the pressure and volume values of the gas after the transformation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Robert Boyle.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The volume of a given amount of gas held at a constant temperature varies inversely with pressure.
 
• The relationship between pressure and volume of Boyle s Law is convey in mathematical terms as P₁V₁=P₂V₂.
 
• The volume of gas is oppositely proportional to the pressure.​
 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ = constant (eq.1)

 P₁ = constant / V1 (eq.2)

 P₁ = constant (1/ V1) (eq.3) / where P is the pressure, V is the volume, the initial state before and the final state after the pressure-volume change, resp.

 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __
 
• **Joseph Gay Lussac:**__

 __
 
• **​**__He discovered the relationship between **the pressure of a gas **and** its absolute temperature.**
 
 
 
• __**​Amedeo Avogadro:**__
 __
 
• **​​**__This is also known as **Avogadro's Law.**
 
 
 
• __**John Dalton:**__
 
• __**​**__The first recognize the total pressure of a mixture of gases is the sum of the contributions of the individual components of the mixture.
